title: Subprocessor Forensics Preservation & Court Safeguard Protocol (Draft)
content:
PURPOSE
This draft playbook defines operational and legal steps Redwood Inference will take to preserve, collect, and document digital evidence from third-party subprocessors when incident response or legal processes require forensic-grade artifacts. It is focused on defensibility in civil and regulatory proceedings and on minimizing business disruption while preserving customer data protections.

SCOPE
- Applies to all contracts with subprocessors that process customer data or telemetry on behalf of Redwood (hosting, inference, logging, telemetry, observability, backups).
- Intended for use when a forensics preservation request is triggered by: legal hold, regulatory inquiry, litigation, internal escalations for security incidents, or customer evidence requests that escalate legally.
- Not a substitute for the DPA or existing vendor-risk clauses; supplements contractual obligations with operational steps.

PRINCIPLES
1) Least-disruptive preservation: preserve only necessary artifacts to satisfy legal/regulatory needs. Avoid broad, service-stopping freezes where possible.
2) Chain-of-custody and authenticity: maintain clear custody logs, hashing, and tamper-evident packaging of exported artifacts.
3) Evidence minimization & privacy: redact or segregate unrelated customer content where feasible; keep copies encrypted at rest and in transit.
4) Timely communication: notify internal stakeholders, customers (as required by contracts/regulation), and the subprocessor of preservation actions per the agreed timelines.

ROLES & CONTACTS
- Lead Legal Contact: Asha Patel (Data Privacy & Contracts) — primary legal owner for holds.
- Incident Forensics Lead: Liam Chen (Applied ML / Forensics) — validates technical scope and collection plan.
- Vendor Ops Liaison: Mariana Ortiz (Vendor Security) — coordinates with subprocessor counterpart.
- SRE Escalation: Evan Brooks (SRE) — executes or verifies technical preservation steps on infra.
- Custodian (on-demand): delegated engineer at subprocessor responsible for exports.

TRIGGERS FOR PRESERVATION
- Court order, subpoena, or discovery notice naming Redwood or a customer where subprocessor data is relevant.
- Internal legal hold notice issued by Legal.
- High-severity security incident where subprocessor telemetry or logs are needed for root cause and third-party remediation.
- Customer escalation with impending litigation and contractual right to evidence.

CONTRACTUAL PREPARATION (PRE-INCIDENT)
Actions to bake into new and renewed subprocessor agreements:
- Preservation covenant clause: subprocessor agrees to preserve relevant artifacts on notice for a minimum hold window (e.g., 90 days) unless otherwise directed by Redwood Legal.
- Named points of contact and SLA for preservation acknowledgement (max 48 hours).
- Implementation of forensic export capability (standardized export formats, hashing, metadata).
- Right to audit: Redwood reserves audit/discovery rights limited to evidence preservation for specific incidents.
- Chain-of-custody attestation requirement for any exported artifacts.
- Encrypted transfer and storage requirements; KMS key ownership / rotation terms defined where applicable.

IMMEDIATE RESPONSE CHECKLIST (ON NOTICE)
1) Legal determines scope and issues formal preservation notice to vendor (template below).
2) Vendor Ops Liaison opens vendor ticket and requests acknowledgement within 48 hours.
3) Forensics Lead drafts technical collection plan: systems, time windows, log ranges, retention buckets.
4) SRE/Evidence engineer creates snapshot plan (live snapshot, cold backup export, log pull) and hashing approach (SHA-256 baseline).
5) Chain-of-custody form opened and versioned in case management tool (include who accessed, when, why).
6) Export artifacts encrypted with agreed algorithm and key management.
7) Hash values recorded and cross-signed by subprocessor custodian and Redwood witness.
8) Store artifacts in locked evidence repository with access limited to legal + forensics team.

EVIDENCE TYPES (examples)
- System logs (application logs, inference request logs, error traces) with timestamps and timezone metadata.
- Persistent storage snapshots (S3 buckets, object storage manifests) and relevant bucket policies.
- Database exports (rows/collections scoped to time ranges or IDs).
- Container image manifests and runtime metadata (image SHA, node metadata).
- Infrastructure metadata (instance IDs, network flow logs, IAM changes).
- Key management audit entries (KMS access log) where permitted by contract.

CHAIN-OF-CUSTODY TEMPLATE (simplified entry)
- Evidence ID: EVID-YYYYMMDD-XXXX
- Source: vendor-name / resource-path
- Collected by: name, role, organization
- Date/time of collection: ISO8601
- Collection method: live-snapshot | API-export | backup-restore
- Hash (SHA-256): <hex>
- Encryption: AES-256-GCM, KMS key id (if used)
- Witness: name, role (Redwood witness or vendor)
- Comments: free text

REDUCTION & REDACTION GUIDELINES
- Where exports capture multiple customers' data, vendor must provide a mapping table and allow Redwood to request customer-scoped extracts. If vendor cannot produce scoped extracts, full exports may be accepted but Redwood will apply redaction tooling and minimize copies retained.
- Personal data not relevant to scope should be redacted before transfer where feasible. If redaction is not technically possible, mark data as sensitive and limit access accordingly.

SAMPLE PRESERVATION NOTICE LANGUAGE (legal to vendor)
"On behalf of Redwood Inference, please preserve all records, logs, backups, and metadata relating to [scope described: customer id(s), resource ids, time window] effective immediately. Provide written acknowledgement within 48 hours outlining the artifacts preserved, the preservation method, and the expected window for exportability. Redwood reserves the right to request authenticated exported artifacts and to take custody under chain-of-custody protocols."

ESCALATION & DISPUTE PATHS
- If subprocessor refuses or fails to acknowledge within 48 hours: Legal triggers contract breach notice and escalates to vendor account executive and procurement.
- If exportability is technically infeasible: Forensics Lead documents constraints; Legal seeks compromise (e.g., vendor-managed export supervised by Redwood witness).
- If vendor demands law enforcement or national security restrictions: route matter to Legal and escalate to CEO/CISO as needed for assessment of cross-border/legal risk.

RETENTION & RETURN POLICY
- Preserved artifacts remain encrypted in Redwood evidence store for the hold period specified by Legal (default 90 days) unless longer retention is required by litigation/regulatory holds.
- After the hold expires or is released by Legal, return or destruction certified by vendor is required. Certificate of destruction or signed return manifest captured in case file.

POST-INCIDENT REVIEW & CONTRACT REMEDIATION
- Conduct a post-mortem within 30 days: what was preserved, gaps, timeliness, costs, and vendor cooperation score.
- Use findings to update vendor risk rating and remediation plan; consider contract updates for future holds or alternate providers if deficiencies are material.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES / TECHNICAL PATTERNS
- Preferred export formats: newline-delimited JSON for logs, Parquet for large structured datasets, gzipped SQL dump for DB exports.
- Supply vendor-export manifest in a machine-readable schema (CSV or JSONL) including resource, time-range, hash, and export method.
- Timestamp normalization: all timestamps in UTC with ISO8601 and noted event-source timezone.
- Hashing: compute checksum over canonical serialization; record canonicalization steps in evidence metadata.

OPEN QUESTIONS (to resolve before finalizing template)
- Standard hold duration for different evidence classes (logs vs. backups).
- KMS ownership model when vendor uses customer-managed keys vs. vendor-managed keys.
- Acceptable redaction techniques and tooling list (in-house vs. third-party).
- Cost recovery model for vendor export effort (when to invoice Redwood).

NEXT STEPS
- Legal to finalize minimal preservation clause language for inclusion in new subprocessor agreements (owner: Asha).
- Vendor Security to run tabletop with top 5 vendors to validate export mechanics (owner: Mariana).
- Forensics to produce canonical evidence manifest schema and sample scripts for verification (owner: Liam).
- Procurement to add preservation acknowledgement SLA into procurement checklist (owner: Evan).

APPENDIX: QUICK CHECKLIST FOR VENDOR OPS (actionable)
- [ ] Acknowledge preservation notice within 48 hrs.
- [ ] Identify custodial resources and contact.
- [ ] Produce manifest of affected artifacts and estimated export timeline.
- [ ] Execute export with hashing and encryption.
- [ ] Provide signed chain-of-custody entry.
- [ ] Upload artifacts to agreed secure location, send access receipt to Redwood Legal.
- [ ] Confirm destruction/return on release.

DOCUMENT HISTORY
- Draft v0.1 2025-01-15: initial authoring (Asha Patel).
- Draft v0.2 2025-02-02: added technical export formats and checklist (Liam Chen).

END OF DRAFT
